title: Reading Daniel 7

objectives.can: Read the vision of Daniel 7: first-person narrative with חָזֵה הֲוֵית, participles, and visionary vocabulary.

explanation.summary: Daniel 7 is the last chapter in Aramaic. It is a vision told by Daniel in the first person: four beasts rise from the sea, thrones are set, and one 'like a son of man' comes before the Ancient of Days. The grammar is ordinary, with a few habits that carry the whole chapter: a participle with the perfect of 'be' for what Daniel was watching, 'behold', comparisons with כְּ, and passive verbs for what was done to the beasts.

sections.heading: From the narrator to Daniel's own voice
body: The chapter opens in the third person: בִּשְׁנַת חֲדָה לְבֵלְאשַׁצַּר מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל דָּנִיֵּאל חֵלֶם חֲזָה, 'in the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon Daniel saw a dream'. The verb חֲזָה is a Peal perfect, third person masculine singular. In the same verse the dream is written down. Then 7:2 begins with the familiar formula עָנֵה דָנִיֵּאל וְאָמַר, 'Daniel answered and said', and from here the visionary speaks as 'I'. So the first-person verbs of the chapter belong to Daniel, speaking inside the quotation.

The visions are placed in time with simple phrases: בְּחֶזְוִי עִם לֵילְיָא, 'in my vision by night' (7:2), and בְּחֶזְוֵי לֵילְיָא, 'in the visions of the night' (7:7, 7:13). The noun in בְּחֶזְוִי has the suffix 'my'; in the other two places the noun is in the construct state.

sections.heading: חָזֵה הֲוֵית: what Daniel was watching
body: Again and again Daniel says חָזֵה הֲוֵית (7:2, 7:4, 7:6, 7:7, 7:9, 7:13). חָזֵה is a Peal participle, masculine singular, 'seeing'. הֲוֵית is the perfect of the verb 'be' (the corpus files it under הָוָא) in the first person singular, 'I was'. Together they make a periphrastic expression: 'I was watching' or 'I kept looking'. The participle describes what goes on; the perfect of 'be' puts it in the past. The same pattern appears for the one who comes in 7:13: אָתֵה הֲוָה, 'was coming', with the third person הֲוָה.

Often the watching is followed by עַד דִּי, 'until': in 7:9 חָזֵה הֲוֵית עַד דִּי כָרְסָוָן רְמִיו, 'I was watching until thrones were set'. The vision is told as a sequence in which Daniel watches and something happens at the end of his watching.

sections.heading: 'Behold', comparisons and what the beasts have
body: The pattern of the descriptions is: 'behold' + what appears + a comparison. The particle for 'behold' is וַאֲרוּ (7:2, 7:5, 7:6, 7:7) or וַאֲלוּ (7:8): 'and behold'. The comparison is made with the prefix כְּ, 'like': כְאַרְיֵה, 'like a lion' (7:4), כֶּאֱנָשׁ, 'like a man' (7:4), כִּנְמַר, 'like a leopard' (7:6). The first beast is said to be קַדְמָיְתָא, 'the first', and the second in 7:5 is called תִנְיָנָה, 'second'.

What the beasts have is said with לְ and a suffix, 'to it': וְגַפִּין דִּי נְשַׁר לַהּ (7:4), literally 'and wings of an eagle to it', which means 'and it had eagle's wings'. In 7:6, וְלַהּ גַּפִּין אַרְבַּע, 'and it had four wings'; in 7:7, וְשִׁנַּיִן דִּי פַרְזֶל לַהּ רַבְרְבָן, 'and it had great teeth of iron'. Aramaic has no verb 'to have' in these sentences: it says the thing is 'to' the owner. The suffix is feminine, because the beast, חֵיוָה, is feminine.

sections.heading: Passive verbs: what was done to the beasts
body: Many verbs of the vision are passive. In 7:4 the wings 'were plucked', דִּי מְּרִיטוּ גַפַּיהּ, the beast 'was lifted' from the earth, וּנְטִילַת מִן אַרְעָא, and 'was made to stand' on two feet: וְעַל רַגְלַיִן כֶּאֱנָשׁ הֳקִימַת, with the Hophal perfect הֳקִימַת, and 'a human heart was given to it', וּלְבַב אֱנָשׁ יְהִיב לַהּ. The verb יְהִיב is a Peil perfect (the passive of the Peal), third person masculine singular, because 'heart' is masculine. The same form comes with 'dominion was given to it' in 7:6 and in 7:14. In 7:9 the Peil perfect plural רְמִיו says that thrones 'were set', and in 7:10 פְּתִיחוּ says that the books 'were opened'.

A passive verb hides who acts. The text leaves the agent unnamed and lets the reader notice that someone gives dominion and opens books. In 7:5 the speakers are not named either: וְכֵן אָמְרִין לַהּ, 'and thus they say to it', a plural participle that means 'it was told' or 'they said'. The speech that follows is two feminine singular imperatives, קוּמִי אֲכֻלִי, 'arise, eat', addressed to the beast, which is feminine.

sections.heading: Thrones, the Ancient of Days and the one like a son of man
body: In 7:9–10 Daniel describes a figure on a throne. He is called עַתִּיק יוֹמִין, word for word 'advanced in days', the sense being an aged one; the English tradition says 'Ancient of Days'. His clothing is כִּתְלַג חִוָּר, 'like white snow', and the hair of his head כַּעֲמַר נְקֵא, 'like clean wool'. A stream of fire comes from before him (7:10); אֶלֶף אַלְפִין, 'a thousand thousands', serve him and a myriad of myriads stand before him. These numbers are plural nouns and show how Aramaic builds large figures.

In 7:13 another figure comes: וַאֲרוּ עִם עֲנָנֵי שְׁמַיָּא כְּבַר אֱנָשׁ אָתֵה הֲוָה, 'and behold, with the clouds of heaven one like a son of man was coming'. The words כְּבַר אֱנָשׁ mean literally 'like a son of a man', that is, like a human being. Who or what this figure is, and what the title means in the chapter, has long been debated, and the debate is not settled by grammar. The words also say that this figure reached the עַתִּיק יוֹמַיָּא (וְעַד עַתִּיק יוֹמַיָּא מְטָה), and that dominion, honour and a kingdom were given to him (7:14): וְלֵהּ יְהִיב שָׁלְטָן וִיקָר וּמַלְכוּ. 'All peoples, nations and languages' serve him, וְכֹל עַמְמַיָּא אֻמַיָּא וְלִשָּׁנַיָּא לֵהּ יִפְלְחוּן, and his dominion is 'an everlasting dominion' דִּי לָא יֶעְדֵּה, 'which will not pass away'. Here דִּי is a relative whose clause has a negated imperfect.

misunderstandings: Reading חָזֵה הֲוֵית as two separate statements, 'I see; I was'. It is one expression: 'I was watching'. The same goes for אָתֵה הֲוָה, 'he was coming'.
Looking for a verb 'to have' in וְלַהּ גַּפִּין אַרְבַּע. The sentence has none: it says 'to it, four wings'.
Translating the passive verbs as active. יְהִיב, רְמִיו and פְּתִיחוּ say that something 'was given', 'were set' and 'were opened'. The agent is left unnamed.

Treating כְּבַר אֱנָשׁ or עַתִּיק יוֹמִין as technical names that the grammar can explain. They are plain phrases, 'like a son of man' and 'advanced in days', and what they refer to is a matter of interpretation, with several views.

deeper.heading: Why the title is disputed
body: The phrase 'son of man' is an ordinary way of saying 'a human being' in both Hebrew and Aramaic, and in Daniel 7 the word כְּ makes it a comparison: the figure is 'like' a human being, in contrast to the beasts. Some readers take the figure as an individual, others as a symbol for a people, and others as an angelic being. This lesson reports that the question exists and does not decide it.

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: Daniel spoke and said: I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the heaven broke forth upon the great sea.
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

examples.analysis: עָנֵה and וְאָמַר are the formula: two Peal participles, and Daniel now speaks. חָזֵה הֲוֵית is the periphrastic expression, a participle with the perfect of 'be': 'I was watching'. וַאֲרוּ, 'behold', announces what he sees.

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: The first was like a lion, and had eagle's wings; I beheld till the wings thereof were plucked off, and it was lifted up from the earth, and made stand upon two feet as a man, and a man's heart was given to it.
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

examples.analysis: The beast is described by comparison with the prefix כְּ: כְאַרְיֵה. 'It had eagle's wings' is said as 'wings of an eagle to it', with לַהּ. Two passive verbs follow: הֳקִימַת, a Hophal perfect, and יְהִיב, a Peil perfect, 'was given'.

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: I beheld till thrones were placed, and one that was ancient of days did sit: his raiment was as white snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, and the wheels thereof burning fire.
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

examples.analysis: חָזֵה הֲוֵית עַד דִּי gives 'I was watching until'. The Peil perfect רְמִיו is passive, 'thrones were set', and עַתִּיק יוֹמִין, with the verb יְתִב, 'sat', names the one on the throne. His clothing is described with the prefix כְּ.

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: I saw in the night visions, and, behold, there came with the clouds of heaven one like unto a son of man, and he came even to the Ancient of days, and he was brought near before Him.
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

examples.analysis: וַאֲרוּ, 'behold', and then the one who comes: כְּבַר אֱנָשׁ is literally 'like a son of a man'. אָתֵה הֲוָה is the same periphrastic pattern as חָזֵה הֲוֵית, 'was coming', now in the third person. The prepositions עִם, 'with', and עַד, 'up to', show the movement; מְטָה is a Peal perfect, 'reached'.

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him; his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

examples.analysis: יְהִיב is a Peil perfect, 'was given', with three subjects: dominion, honour and a kingdom. The peoples, nations and languages are the subject of the imperfect יִפְלְחוּן, 'will serve', and the two דִּי clauses with לָא describe the dominion as one that 'will not pass away'.

quoted.title: Daniel
quoted.english: And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him; his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

options: It will pass away to another
It is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away
It was given and taken back
It is a dominion of the ancient time that has gone
check.explain: שָׁלְטָן עָלַם is 'a dominion of perpetuity', and the relative דִּי with לָא and the Peal imperfect יֶעְדֵּה adds 'which will not pass away'.

reading.why: The first fourteen verses of the vision: the setting, the four beasts, the thrones, the Ancient of Days and the one like a son of man. They hold חָזֵה הֲוֵית, 'behold', comparisons, passive verbs and possession with לְ.

segments.title: Daniel
segments.english: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon Daniel had a dream and visions of his head upon his bed; then he wrote the dream and told the sum of the matters.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Daniel
segments.english: Daniel spoke and said: I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the heaven broke forth upon the great sea.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Daniel
segments.english: And four great beasts came up from the sea, diverse one from another.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Daniel
segments.english: The first was like a lion, and had eagle's wings; I beheld till the wings thereof were plucked off, and it was lifted up from the earth, and made stand upon two feet as a man, and a man's heart was given to it.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Daniel
segments.english: And behold another beast, a second, like to a bear, and it raised up itself on one side, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth; and it was said thus unto it: 'Arise, devour much flesh.'
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Daniel
segments.english: After this I beheld, and lo another, like a leopard, which had upon the sides of it four wings of a fowl; the beast had also four heads; and dominion was given to it.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Daniel
segments.english: After this I saw in the night visions, and behold a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth; it devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet; and it was diverse from all the beasts that were before it; and it had ten horns.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Daniel
segments.english: I considered the horns, and, behold, there came up among them another horn, a little one, before which three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots; and, behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking great things.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Daniel
segments.english: I beheld till thrones were placed, and one that was ancient of days did sit: his raiment was as white snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, and the wheels thereof burning fire.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Daniel
segments.english: A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him; thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him; the judgment was set, and the books were opened.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Daniel
segments.english: I beheld at that time because of the voice of the great words which the horn spoke, I beheld even till the beast was slain, and its body destroyed, and it was given to be burned with fire.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Daniel
segments.english: And as for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was taken away; yet their lives were prolonged for a season and a time.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Daniel
segments.english: I saw in the night visions, and, behold, there came with the clouds of heaven one like unto a son of man, and he came even to the Ancient of days, and he was brought near before Him.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

Every Aramaic word shown as an example, in a paradigm or in an exercise is taken from the Aramaic of the Westminster Leningrad Codex as analysed by the Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible project.
